Thought: The mass spectrometry data provides several peaks with their respective m/z (mass-to-charge) ratios and intensities. The most intense peak, often referred to as the base peak, is at m/z 198.9997. This is likely the molecular ion peak, which represents the molecular weight of the compound. The other peaks are likely isotopic variants or fragments. Based on the m/z value of the base peak, I can deduce the molecular formula.

The m/z value of 198.9997 suggests the presence of elements with specific isotopic patterns. The small differences in m/z values around 200 suggest the presence of chlorine (Cl) or bromine (Br), which have characteristic isotopic patterns. Given the m/z value, it is likely that the compound contains chlorine, as bromine would result in a higher m/z value for the molecular ion.

The molecular formula that fits this m/z value and isotopic pattern is likely C7H5ClO. This formula has a molecular weight close to 198.9997, considering the isotopic contribution of chlorine.
